note: The repository-owned expectation manifest for the corrected CWE-916 query. Every fixture case is named, and every case says whether a finding is expected and why. The guard compares the exact set of case ids against what `codeql test run` actually produced: an extra finding and a missing finding both fail. Counting rows would not catch a case that stopped alerting while another started.
identifiedBy: The function enclosing the flow's source, with the source lines pinned from the CLI's own output. Several cases share one digest site, so the sink does not identify a case; the source always does. MUT-MIXED-PASSWORD has two source lines because it has two password-classified sources: the minting call and the password beside it.

cases.rationale: A password is digested with SHA-1. The premise of the rule holds exactly: a small search space behind a cheap digest.
SHA-256 is no more expensive to enumerate than SHA-1 when the input is a password.
A key does not enlarge a password's search space. Keying is what the correction accepts for a credential, so this case pins that keying alone never exempts a password.
Material derived from a password by a template carries the password's entropy, not more.
A password folded into a request fingerprint is still a password reaching a fast digest.
Passing through helper functions and an object property changes nothing about the value.
Aliases, an array join and a template are all shapes the correction tolerates for a credential; none of them may launder a password.

The opaque-credential contour step for step — argument to parameter, `?? ''`, String(), array, join, keyed HMAC — with a password in place of the token. If the correction ever keyed on the shape rather than on the entropy, this is the flow that would disappear.
The token is never minted: it arrives from the request body. Nothing establishes it as credential material, so the first condition of the barrier fails and the digest is reported.
The draw is 8 bytes, below the authority's 32-byte minimum, so it is not accepted as credential material. A weakened issuer must be reported again.
The key is the very pre-image it is meant to protect, so one draw feeds both and the key condition fails. A digest keyed by its own input is not a keyed digest.
The purpose is taken from the request, so an attacker chooses a label in the pre-image. It is not a fixed purpose and does not count toward domain separation.
Same as the purpose case, for the version label: attacker-chosen, therefore not a fixed authority version.
A bare hash is not a keyed digest, so the digest condition fails however good the token is.

The token beside it is genuinely opaque, but a password shares the pre-image. Not every source is a minting call, so the digest stays reported — this is the case that would be masked by a barrier keyed on the token alone.
32 bytes straight from a CSPRNG into a keyed digest. There is no enumerable space for a digest cost to bound.
A 256-bit bearer token assembled from random parts; assembly preserves the entropy it was drawn with.
Purpose-bound, versioned, keyed digest of a freshly minted credential. The name contains the word password; the value is not one.
Same shape under the mfa-recovery purpose, which digests differently from every other purpose.
Refresh tokens are verified on every rotation; a slow KDF here would add latency and a denial-of-service surface without adding protection.
Same reasoning as the refresh token, on the login critical path.
Purpose-bound digest of a minted invitation credential.
Purpose-bound digest of a minted verification credential.
The wrapper whose name produced the original false positive. It renames fields and mints nothing itself.
The mint site: two CSPRNG draws assembled into a token and digested once, under a fixed purpose and version.
A password-named issuer returning an object with the token inside it. The name is the whole of the rule's evidence; the callee demonstrably draws credential material.

The verification path, where the token arrives from outside as a string and is split, reassembled and digested again. No CSPRNG call appears anywhere along it, which is why a barrier phrased as a local property of the value could not close it.
Issue and verify joined, which is the flow the analysis reports on the product. This is the case that must stay silent for the product finding to be zero.
